name: Eleven-Vertex Edge-and-Square Attachment Core
definition: In four coordinates with weights $1,2,4,8$, take $S=\{0,1,2,3,7,8,9,11,12,13,15\}$ and mark the edge $T=\{0,8\}$. Equivalently, expand the punctured cube $\{0,1,2,3,4,5,7\}$ so that complementary components $\{2\}$ and $\{4,5\}$ lie on opposite sides of the reduction path $0-1-3-7$.
parameters: $S$ has $11$ concepts, $16$ edges, and four active coordinates. Its three marked horizontal squares are $(0,1,2,3)$, $(8,9,12,13)$, and $(9,11,13,15)$.
properties: $S$ is ample and corner-peelable. Among all $2^{16}=65536$ orientations, exactly $784$ are acyclic USOs; $69$ have sink $0$, $69$ have sink $8$, and $72$ retain the target edge. The two endpoint records have $79$ distinct common attachment-constraint signatures, each covered by a target-retaining map. The coordinate-$8$ reduction is the four-vertex path $0-1-3-7$.
